title: Migration 70 — the read-only auditing role may read the evidence chain
description: Builds the world production was in on 2026-08-12: status_history with its pre-63 policies (including the RESTRICTIVE overlay from migration 22) followed by 63 itself, then 64, 65, 67, 68 and 69 to construct the evidence chain, then a pre-apply stage that creates the two auditing roles and reproduces compliance_audit_log's measured policies and the SELECT grants both roles ALREADY HELD. That last detail is the point: the grant was never missing. Every read was refused because the only SELECT policy on each table called is_ddp_admin() and was applied to PUBLIC, so it was planned for a role holding no EXECUTE on it. Measured on PostgreSQL 17.10, neither amending that predicate nor adding a second permissive policy fixes it — PostgreSQL permission-checks every function in every APPLICABLE policy at plan time, so OR never short-circuits. 70 therefore re-scopes the blocking policies to `authenticated`, where their auth.uid()-derived predicates always belonged, and adds one auditor policy per table. VERIFY B becomes each auditing role and reads a probe row from all five tables; C proves the admin, non-admin and farm-member paths still behave exactly as before, which is the section that fails if a re-created predicate was mangled; D proves the role still cannot write. Rollback restores all six policies to PUBLIC verbatim — the harness snapshots each policy's roles alongside its qual, so a rollback that dropped only the auditor policies and left the re-scope in place would be caught here rather than shipped.

verify.note: A structural: the five auditor policies exist on PUBLIC, and — the real discriminator — no OTHER policy on these tables that is planned for a SELECT is still applied to PUBLIC, because one that is would be planned for the auditing roles and would error no matter how correct the auditor policy is. B behavioural: SET ROLE to each auditing role in turn and read a specific probe row from all five tables. Asserting visibility rather than absence-of-error is deliberate — granting EXECUTE on is_ddp_admin() would also stop the error and then return zero rows for ever, and a no-exception check would have passed that broken fix. C behavioural, in both directions: an admin still reads all five, a non-admin still reads none, and a farm member still sees their own farm's status history and not another farm's — 70 re-creates six live predicates by hand and this is where a mangled one shows. D behavioural: the auditing role still cannot INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE. E the apply recorded itself in the ledger. F neither auditing role owns a SECURITY DEFINER function, which is the standing condition that makes the current_user string comparison safe. That this VERIFY actually FAILS once 70 is rolled back is not asserted by any key in this fixture — the harness has no such key, and inventing one would be a claim nothing checks. It is proven separately by re-running the VERIFY against a rolled-back cluster; see the handover.
